sections.h2: Where is Lexington, SC, and what is the town like?
sections.html:
Lexington is the county seat of Lexington County and the county's most populous town, about 12 miles west of Columbia. It sits in the northeastern part of the county at an elevation of roughly 315 feet.

The town covers about 12 square miles. Fourteenmile Creek drains the north side and Twelvemile Creek the south, and both flow northeast into the Saluda River. Lake Murray lies just north of town, and U.S. Route 1 (Augusta Highway) runs through it.

Wikipedia describes Lexington as a suburb of Columbia, and the town's growth since 2000 follows that pattern. Sellers here usually deal with buyers comparing the lake, the school zone and drive time into Columbia.

sections.h2: What is the history of Lexington, and why does the courthouse town look the way it does?
sections.html:
Lexington began as part of a 1735 colonial township plan, and the name Lexington County replaced Saxe Gotha in 1785 in honor of the battles of Lexington and Concord. Granby was the county seat until chronic flooding moved the courthouse to Lexington in 1820.

The town was incorporated in 1861. Union forces destroyed much of it during the Carolinas campaign, including the courthouse, and fires in 1894 and 1916 led to many of the brick buildings that stand today. Growth picked up with the Columbia to Augusta railroad and the Lexington Textile Mill in the 1890s, then with suburban expansion once cars became common.

The result is a mix of older downtown properties and newer subdivisions. Population went from 9,793 in 2000 to 17,870 in 2010 and 23,568 in 2020. Newer subdivisions sit alongside the older core, so condition varies widely from street to street.

sections.h2: How does Lake Murray affect Lexington property?
sections.html:
Lake Murray is the town's best known feature and it influences nearby property values and buyer interest. The lake was created in 1930 and is held back by a dam about 1.7 miles long, about 5 miles north of town.

The dam roadway is open for driving, biking, running and walking, and a public swimming area operates on the Lexington side in summer. A house near the lake may come with water access questions, dock permits and flood zone paperwork that other Lexington houses never touch. We did not confirm lake permitting rules from an official page, so ask the owner of the shoreline, the county and your title company what applies to your parcel.

sections.h2: What drives the Lexington economy and the school district?
sections.html:
Lexington's economy leans on public employers and retail. Town retail sales were nearly $2.5 billion in 2022, and the largest employers in the town's 2020 financial report were:

  • Lexington School District 1, 1,083 employees
  • Lexington County, 905
  • Walmart, 367
  • Town of Lexington, 180
  • Publix, 160

Lexington County School District One serves the town, with more than 27,000 students. Its high schools are Lexington, River Bluff and White Knoll. Families often choose a house by school zone, so a seller whose home is zoned to a sought-after school has one more point to mention to buyers.

COMET, the Central Midlands Regional Transit Authority, provides public transit. In 2019 SC Highway 6 (Lake Drive) and Church Street became one-way streets downtown, and an overpass across Interstate 20 is a planned project.

sections.h2: How does the Lexington climate affect a house?
sections.html:
Lexington has hot summers and mild winters, and the heat is the main stress on roofs and cooling systems. Columbia airport normals for 1981 to 2010 list a July average high of 93 degrees and a January average low of 30 degrees.

The annual precipitation average is 44.56 inches, with July the wettest month, and snowfall averages 1.6 inches. The record high is 109 degrees. A roof and HVAC unit that have gone through many of these summers deserve a close look before a sale.

sections.h2: What does the Town of Lexington require for permits and code issues?
sections.html:
The Town's Planning and Building Department handles permits, inspections, zoning and code enforcement. It is at 111 Maiden Lane, open Monday to Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., with the main line at 803-356-5938. Inspections are scheduled at 803-358-7267 and code enforcement is at 803-358-1589.

The department also reviews proposed businesses for land use compliance during business license approval, and supports the Board of Zoning Appeals, the Building Codes Board of Appeals, the Board of Appearance and the Planning Commission. If you plan a repair before selling, check whether it needs a permit. Unpermitted work can slow a conventional sale.

A Lexington mailing address does not always mean the parcel is inside the town limits. Confirm with the town whether your parcel is in town before you choose an office to call.

sections.h2: How do Lexington County taxes and recording work for a sale?
sections.html:
Lexington County bills the tax and the county Register of Deeds records the deed. State law sets taxes as due between September 30 and January 15, adds a 3% penalty after January 15, then another 7% after February 1 and 5% after March 16. A legal residence is assessed at 4% and other real property at 6%.

Lexington County runs an optional installment program for real property. Five advance payments of 16.67% of the prior year's tax are due February 15, April 15, June 15, August 15 and October 15, and the balance is due January 15. The application must be received before January 15. Escrowed taxes and personal vehicles are excluded.

The Register of Deeds is at 212 S. Lake Dr., Suite 301, and records deeds, mortgages, liens and plats. Since March 1, 2018, an affidavit is required for taxable or exempt transfers. Documents must not include Social Security or bank account numbers unless the law requires them. Records are searchable online from August 1, 1984, and e-recording runs through partners such as Simplifile and CSC. The state deed fee is $1.85 per $500 of value.

sections.h2: What Lexington sellers often face before listing
sections.html:
Sellers in Lexington often run into the same few hurdles when they try a traditional listing:

  • Repairs a buyer's inspector will flag, such as an aging roof or cooling system
  • Unpermitted work that the Town's building department may ask about
  • Estate or probate timing when an owner has died
  • Back taxes or penalties after the January 15 due date

Each of these can be handled in a cash sale, because we buy the house as it stands. Back taxes are usually settled at closing through the title company.

sections.h2: What does a cash sale look like for a Lexington house?
sections.html:
A cash sale skips the lender, the appraisal and the repair negotiation. You tell us about the house, we review it as it stands, and you choose a closing date with a title company.

We buy houses with deferred repairs, inherited houses and houses with tenants. We cannot promise a price in advance, and you owe nothing if you decline the offer.

faqs.q: What county is Lexington, SC in?
faqs.a: Lexington is the county seat of Lexington County. The county handles tax bills and deed recording, while the town handles zoning, permits and code enforcement inside its limits.

faqs.q: When are Lexington County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due between September 30 and January 15 under state law. After January 15, a 3% penalty applies, with 7% more after February 1 and 5% more after March 16.

faqs.q: Can I pay Lexington County property taxes in installments?
faqs.a: Yes, through the county's optional installment program. You must apply before January 15, and escrowed taxes are excluded. Five payments of 16.67% of last year's tax come due February 15 through October 15.

faqs.q: What does it take to record a deed in Lexington County?
faqs.a: You need a deed and an affidavit for taxable or exempt transfers, plus the state fee of $1.85 per $500 of value. The Register of Deeds office is at 212 S. Lake Dr., Suite 301.

faqs.q: Does Lake Murray change how I sell my Lexington house?
faqs.a: It can. Lake-adjacent parcels may involve shoreline, dock and flood questions that other houses do not, so ask your title company about your parcel.
Lexington County School District One serves the town, with high schools named Lexington, River Bluff and White Knoll. Confirm your address zone with the district.
